entries.question: What is TinyML and why does on-device, milliwatt-scale inference matter?
Why can't an existing ML or embedded benchmark just be used?
What exactly does this paper ask?
What did the authors build, concretely?
How is a fair comparison enforced across very different hardware/software while still allowing innovation?
How exactly is latency/accuracy/energy measured, and what stops someone from gaming the energy number?
For each of the four tasks: why this task, this data, this model, and this pass/fail bar?
Did the suite, once specified, actually run and meet its own targets?
Did anyone outside the authors actually use it, and on what?
What patterns showed up across the round (numerics, frameworks, power)?
Is there anything notable that nobody did?
So, taken together, does the suite answer the research question?
Why would a modular, three-metric design let heterogeneous stacks be compared at all (mechanism)?
What does the round's diversity NOT show?
What are the boundaries the authors themselves place on all of this?
What should a reader remember a day later?
